items.name: permission-editor
items.title: Permission Editor
items.description: A controlled permission editor for one role in up to three tabs: Menus, a checkbox tree of the business menus the role sees with the objects each page uses; Business objects, each object's actions set once with a view scope that other actions follow or narrow; and System settings, each settings page's actions without data scopes, its entry showing while the action that opens it is on. Risky actions are never turned on automatically.
items.docs: Pass menus (a tree of PermissionMenuNode), objects (business objects with their actions) and the role's draft as value { menus, grants }; onChange receives the next draft. Menus only decide sidebar visibility: value.menus lists the checked menu ids, public menus are always checked, and a menu with opensWith is checked exactly when that action is on, for settings pages guarded by an action rather than a page grant. Checking a menu grants nothing. menu.uses names the primary and related objects the page uses; they are shown as reference tags, and a checked menu whose primary object cannot be viewed gets a warning with a button that opens the object. Each object has one setting that applies in every menu that uses it. An action id is present in grants exactly when it is on. Mark the object's View action with view: true and give it the scope slot; other actions' slots with followsView: true show “Same as view (X)” and offer only options that View's own widest-first order, or its narrower map, ranks narrower. A slot that reads another object's records, such as the customers a contract approval checks, sets followsView to that object's View action id: it shows “Same as Customers view (X)”, so each object's scope is set in one place. While that View is off the slot shows its stored value read-only with a Needs X view hint. Opening or saving a role keeps every stored value and shows one wider than View, or one View does not list, as itself. Only narrowing View, or turning on the View a slot follows, sends followers not provably narrower, in any object, back to Same as view, with a notice; widening View keeps every follower as it is. On narrow containers the three tabs wrap onto more lines so every name and count stays readable. Actions require the object's View action unless requires lists others; turning one on turns its requirements on transitively, and an action whose chain reaches a risky or managed action still off stays off with a notice. Turning one off asks before turning off what needs it. risk: high or sensitive actions carry no tag and are never turned on by Enable all or as a requirement. Pass unrestricted for a role such as Administrator. Use header for the role name and host actions such as Duplicate as new role, footer for Discard and Save, and object.notice for warnings such as who can grant access. Label extra scope slots with the registered title of the object they filter. A slot's configuration, such as a custom filter, is read-only while the slot follows a View; when the host changes what View's value means, such as its filter conditions, it calls capFollowers and shows the notices. The host converts stored grants to this draft and back, and owns loading, validation and Save. Build objects from the application's implemented operations: one action per independently assignable operation, never invented CRUD or a bundled Manage action. These are rules of the draft; the server still enforces every action and scope. Existing applications move to this version through a source upgrade of the component, the model and their adapter. See the authorization Registry README.

items.name: role-list
items.title: Role List
items.description: A role administration table built with the standard DataTable: localized column headers, sortable names and identifiers, protected/custom badges, and pagination. The host supplies authorized rows and edit destinations. Preinstalled in both application templates.
items.docs: Render inside a React Router and the application i18n provider. Supply roles with key, localized title, edit destination (to) and protected state. Pass localized labels for name, key, type, protected and custom, plus an optional ariaLabel. Uses the shared DataTable for table semantics, sorting and pagination. Optional tableState accepts controlled pagination/sorting and page-size choices from the host URL adapter. The host owns loading, empty/error states, filtering and authorization; pass loading={active && request.loading && listState === 'ready'} so a same-query refresh shows the table's standard refresh indicator while a refresh-failure retry is announced only by its retry button. Existing apps must update the installed role-list component, its data-table dependency and caller labels together.

items.name: default-access-editor
items.title: Default Access Editor
items.description: Controlled default data scope fields grouped by operation, with independently named ranges and native custom-filter slots. The host supplies localized business captions, current rules and authorized writes.
items.docs: Pass localized labels, a stable rule key, resource choices and scope controls. Explain that default data scopes combine with role-granted scopes for users who already hold the operation permission, and that restriction rules still constrain final access. The host loads authorization/defaultAccess and authorization/defaultAccess/options, enforces settings:authorization.default-access read/create/update/delete, and owns draft preservation, custom filters, validation, confirmation and writes. Existing apps reconcile the editor, default-access pages/model/routes, locales from the updated template. No existing rule is seeded or rewritten on upgrade. Both templates expose one Permission management sidebar entry with Roles and permissions and Default data scopes tabs, without changing their route ids, URLs, settings guards or stored rules. This navigation organization does not add sharing or restriction editors. Keep global default data scopes in the Permission management tabs and omit the contextual shortcut from role editors to avoid confusing global rules with the current role’s scopes. Group scopes with the same stable actionId under one operation heading; each scope retains its independent id, selection, filter and error. The application shares scope captions with its role permission adapter rather than exposing collection identifiers, and preserves original resource/action/scope keys and stored rules.
